raw_case_text:
A 38-year-old male durian farm owner in Thailand with no previous medical history developed reduced visual acuity in both of his eyes for 3 days before presenting to our hospital. It was preceded by a headache, which led him to his local hospital after a week. No neurological deficits were found at the time but further investigation with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain showed a 2-cm heterogeneous enhancing cystic lesion at the right thalamus (Fig. 1). The provisional diagnosis was a brain tumour. He was hospitalised and received intravenous dexamethasone at 8 mg per day and pethidine for the pain. He later developed reduced vision of the left eye 8 days after receiving the treatment. Declining acuity of the right eye was noted over the following 2 days. He self-referred to our hospital for further management.
His initial examination showed diffuse erythematous umbilicated pustules. Neurological examination showed reduced visual acuity: on the right eye was a finger count at 1 foot with intact visual field and no light perception in the left eye. Both pupils were 5 millimetres and only slightly reactive to light with relative afferent pupillary reflex on the left. Fundoscopic examination was normal with no papilloedema. Resting eye position was in midline but with impaired eye movement in all directions in both eyes. Other cranial nerve examinations revealed right upper motor neuron facial weakness, reduced left gag reflex.
Another MRI of the brain was done 2 weeks after the previous MRI and showed a similar cystic lesion, probably cryptococcoma (Fig. 1). Other positive MRI findings were multiple enlarged perivascular spaces involving bilateral basal ganglia, probably gelatinous pseudocysts with leptomeningeal enhancement and abnormal peri-optic enhancement. CT scan of the chest with contrast showed a 4x3x2-cm well-defined, irregular-shaped, non-enhancing mass at the lateral segment of the right middle lobe.
Lumbar puncture showed colourless CSF with opening pressure of 60 cmH2O, closing pressure of 40 cmH2O, WBC 56 cells/uL (Polymorphonuclear cell 8.9 %, Lymphocyte 91.1 %), RBC 0 cell/uL, protein 48.6 mg/dL, glucose 69 mg/dL (random blood sugar 151 mg/dL). Cryptococcal antigen was positive with a titer of 1:2048 and encapsulated budding yeast was seen from India ink examination (Fig. 2). CSF fungal culture revealed Cryptococcus gattii. Wright's stain of a chest papule was also positive for budding yeast. His anti-HIV testing was negative and his immunoglobulin levels were within normal limits.
The diagnosis of cryptococcal meningoencephalitis with disseminated Cryptococcus gattii was established and he was started on Amphotericin B 0.75 mg/kg/day with flucytosine 12 g/day and underwent surgery for a ventriculoperitoneal shunt. His visual acuity and eye movement improved partially after 10 days of treatment initiation, and he was transferred back to his local hospital to complete his treatment.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 38-year-old Thai male durian farm owner presented with a 3-day history of severe bilateral visual loss preceded by a 3-week headache and 10 days of intravenous dexamethasone for a suspected right thalamic brain tumor.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Three weeks prior to presentation, the previously healthy patient developed a persistent headache and was found at a local hospital to have a 2-cm ring-enhancing cystic right thalamic lesion on brain MRI. Provisionally diagnosed with a brain tumor and treated with IV dexamethasone (8 mg/day) and pethidine, he developed visual loss in his left eye 8 days into steroid therapy followed 2 days later by visual decline in his right eye, prompting self-referral.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy durian farm owner in Thailand; received 10 days of IV dexamethasone (8 mg/day) prior to referral.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for headache, progressive bilateral visual loss, diplopia/ophthalmoplegia, and diffuse umbilicated skin pustules. Recent medications: IV dexamethasone 8 mg/day and pethidine.

objective.physical_examination: Cutaneous exam showed diffuse erythematous umbilicated pustules (including on the chest). Neuro-ophthalmic exam revealed visual acuity reduced to finger counting at 1 foot OD and no light perception OS, 5-mm sluggishly reactive pupils bilaterally with a left relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD), normal fundoscopy without papilledema, severe bilateral pan-ophthalmoplegia (impaired extraocular movements in all directions), right upper motor neuron facial weakness, and a reduced left gag reflex.
objective.routine_investigations: Random blood glucose 151 mg/dL, negative anti-HIV testing, normal serum immunoglobulin levels, and Wright's stain of a chest umbilicated papule positive for budding yeast.
objective.advanced_workup: Repeat brain MRI demonstrated the 2-cm cystic right thalamic lesion (cryptococcoma) alongside multiple bilateral basal ganglia gelatinous pseudocysts (dilated perivascular spaces), leptomeningeal enhancement, and bilateral peri-optic nerve enhancement. Contrast chest CT revealed a well-defined 4 x 3 x 2 cm non-enhancing mass in the lateral segment of the right middle lobe. Lumbar puncture showed severe intracranial hypertension with opening pressure 60 cmH2O (closing pressure 40 cmH2O), colorless CSF, WBC 56 cells/uL (91.1% lymphocytes, 8.9% PMNs), RBC 0, protein 48.6 mg/dL, glucose 69 mg/dL, positive CSF India ink stain, CSF CrAg titer 1:2048, and CSF fungal culture isolating Cryptococcus gattii.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis of disseminated Cryptococcus gattii infection (meningoencephalitis, right thalamic cryptococcoma, basal ganglia gelatinous pseudocysts, bilateral optic perineuritis, right middle lobe pulmonary cryptococcoma, and umbilicated cutaneous cryptococcosis) exacerbated by empirical dexamethasone in an immunocompetent host, confirmed by CSF India ink microscopy, CSF CrAg titer of 1:2048, CSF fungal culture growing C. gattii, and positive chest papule Wright's stain. Treated with ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement for severe intracranial hypertension (OP 60 cmH2O) and induction therapy with IV amphotericin B (0.75 mg/kg/day) plus oral flucytosine (12 g/day), achieving partial improvement in visual acuity and extraocular motility after 10 days before transfer back to his local hospital to complete therapy.
